newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures sharply lower in late trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures sharply lower in late trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled sharply lower Wednesday after slumping in late trade, but volumes were unimpressive, market sources said.
"Everybody was waiting for new buyers to come in, but they never showed," said one dealer.
As a result, some long positions were liquidated just ahead of the market close, he added.

November California-Oregon border (COB) futures ended at $17.60 per megawatt hour (MWh), down 37 cents. December COB settled 30 cents lower at $18.80. Other forward COB contracts also closed lower on the day.
November Palo Verde (PV) finished at $17.15 per MWh, down 24 cents. December PV settled 29 cents lower at $16.55, while January rose 10 cents to $17.00.
One trader theorized that the electricity futures could see a jump to the upside on Thursday as remaining big longs force price higher ahead of another bout of profit-taking.
